arxiv-1905-09092.title: Time-Delay Polaritonics
arxiv-1905-09092.creator: J. D. Töpfer 1,2∗, H. Sigurdsson 1,2, L. Pickup 2, P. G. Lagoudakis 1,2∗
arxiv-1905-09092.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by J. D. Töpfer 1,2∗, H. Sigurdsson 1,2, L. Pickup 2, P. G. Lagoudakis 1,2∗. Non-linearity and finite signal propagation speeds are omnipresent in nature, technologies, and real-world problems, where efficient ways of describing and predicting the effects of these elements are in high demand. Advances in engineering condensed matter systems, such as lattices of trapped condensates, have enabled studies on non-linear effects in many-body systems where exchange of particles between lattice nodes is effectively instantaneous.

arxiv-1911-07350.title: A dynamical evolution of GRB-Afterglows in a new generic model
arxiv-1911-07350.creator: E Zouaoui and N Mebarki
arxiv-1911-07350.description: Abstract A new model using a general expression of the radiation energy and explaining the dynamics of the afterglows is proposed. It is shown that this model is suitable for the ultra-relativistic and non-relativistic phases as well as the study of radiative and adiabatic fireballs.

arxiv-2107-01204.title: Closed forms of the Zassenhaus formula
arxiv-2107-01204.description: Abstract The Zassenhaus formula finds many applications in theoretical physics or mathematics, from fluid dynamics to differential geometry. The non-commutativity of the elements of the algebra implies that the exponential of a sum of operators cannot be expressed as the product of exponentials of operators.

Characterization of Einstein Poisson warped product space Buddhadev Pal and Pankaj Kumar 1 1 1 The Second author is supported by UGC JRF of India, Ref. No: 1269/(SC)(CSIR-UGC NET DEC. Abstract In this article, we study the problem of the existence and nonexistence of warping function associated with constant scalar curvature on pseudo-Riemannian Poisson warped product space under the assumption that fiber space has constant scalar curvature.

arxiv-2207-02260.title: An A - Φ \Phi Formulation Solver in Electromagnetics Based on Discrete Exterior Calculus Thanks: Thanks:
arxiv-2207-02260.creator: Boyuan Zhang, Dong-Yeop Na, Dan Jiao, Weng Cho Chew
arxiv-2207-02260.description: Abstract An efficient numerical solver for the A - Φ \Phi formulation in electromagnetics based on discrete exterior calculus (DEC) is proposed in this paper. The A - Φ \Phi formulation is immune to low-frequency breakdown and ideal for broadband and multi-scale analysis.

arxiv-2402-08777.title: DNABERT-S: Pioneering Species Differentiation with Species-Aware DNA Embeddings
arxiv-2402-08777.creator: Zhihan Zhou Weimin Wu Harrison Ho Jiayi Wang Lizhen Shi, Ramana V Davuluri Zhong Wang Han Liu
arxiv-2402-08777.description: Abstract We introduce DNABERT-S, a tailored genome model that develops species-aware embeddings to naturally cluster and segregate DNA sequences of different species in the embedding space. Differentiating species from genomic sequences (i.e., DNA and RNA) is vital yet challenging, since many real-world species remain uncharacterized, lacking known genomes for reference.

arxiv-2406-17171.title: Spectrum-preserving Deformations of Integrable Spin Chains with Open Boundaries
arxiv-2406-17171.creator: Yunfeng Jiang, Yuan Miao
arxiv-2406-17171.description: Abstract We discover a family of local deformations that leave part of the spectrum intact for strongly interacting and exactly solvable quantum many-body systems. Since the deformation preserves the Bethe Ansatz equations (BAE), it is dubbed the iso-BAE flow. Although all theories on the flow share the same BAE, the spectra are different.

arxiv-2410-04880.title: Improved detection of discarded fish species through BoxAL active learning
arxiv-2410-04880.creator: Maria Sokolova, Pieter M. Blok, Angelo Mencarelli, Arjan Vroegop, Aloysius van Helmond, Gert Kootstra
arxiv-2410-04880.description: Abstract In recent years, powerful data-driven deep-learning techniques have been developed and applied for automated catch registration. However, these methods are dependent on the labelled data, which is time-consuming, labour-intensive, expensive to collect and need expert knowledge. In this study, we present an active learning technique, named BoxAL, which includes estimation of epistemic certainty of the Faster R-CNN object-detection model.

arxiv-2412-16207.title: Synthetic Time Series Data Generation for Healthcare Applications: A PCG Case Study
arxiv-2412-16207.creator: Ainaz Jamshidi, Muhammad Arif, Sabir Ali Kalhoro, Alexander Gelbukh
arxiv-2412-16207.description: Abstract The generation of high-quality medical time series data is essential for advancing healthcare diagnostics and safeguarding patient privacy. Specifically, synthesizing realistic phonocardiogram (PCG) signals offers significant potential as a cost-effective and efficient tool for cardiac disease pre-screening. Despite its potential, the synthesis of PCG signals for this specific application received limited attention in research.

arxiv-2504-06888.title: The Singular CR Yamabe Problem and Hausdorff Dimension
arxiv-2504-06888.creator: Sagun Chanillo, Paul C. Yang
arxiv-2504-06888.description: Abstract In this paper we consider CR analogs of Huber’s theorem for Riemann surfaces. We also investigate the developing map for CR structures that are spherical in the case of three dimensional CR manifolds and give conditions when this developing map is injective.

arxiv-2509-00083.title: Data Cartography for Detecting Memorization Hotspots and Guiding Data Interventions in Generative Models
arxiv-2509-00083.creator: Laksh Patel, Neel Shanbhag
arxiv-2509-00083.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Laksh Patel, Neel Shanbhag. Modern generative models risk overfitting and unintentionally memorizing rare training examples, which can be extracted by adversaries or inflate benchmark performance. We propose Generative Data Cartography (GenDataCarto) , a data-centric framework that assigns each pretraining sample a difficulty score (early-epoch loss) and a memorization score (frequency of “forget events”), then partitions examples into four quadrants to guide targeted pruning and up-/down-weighting.

arxiv-2509-07477.title: MedicalPatchNet: A Patch-Based Self-Explainable AI Architecture for Chest X-ray Classification
arxiv-2509-07477.creator: Patrick Wienholt, Christiane Kuhl, Jakob Nikolas Kather, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn
arxiv-2509-07477.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Patrick Wienholt, Christiane Kuhl, Jakob Nikolas Kather, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn. Deep neural networks excel in radiological image classification but frequently suffer from poor interpretability, limiting clinical acceptance. We present MedicalPatchNet, an inherently self-explainable architecture for chest X-ray classification that transparently attributes decisions to distinct image regions. MedicalPatchNet splits images into non-overlapping patches, independently classifies each patch, and aggregates predictions, enabling intuitive visualization of each patch’s diagnostic contribution without post-hoc techniques.

arxiv-2601-14777.title: FunCineForge: A Unified Dataset Toolkit and Model for Zero-Shot Movie Dubbing in Diverse Cinematic Scenes
arxiv-2601-14777.creator: Jiaxuan Liu, Yang Xiang, Han Zhao, Xiangang LiZhenhua Ling
arxiv-2601-14777.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jiaxuan Liu, Yang Xiang, Han Zhao, Xiangang LiZhenhua Ling. Movie dubbing is the task of synthesizing speech from scripts conditioned on video scenes, requiring accurate lip sync, faithful timbre transfer, and proper modeling of character identity and emotion.

arxiv-2602-05035.title: Capacity Constraints and the Multilingual Penalty for Lexical Disambiguation
arxiv-2602-05035.creator: Sean Trott, Pamela D. Rivière
arxiv-2602-05035.description: Abstract Multilingual language models (LMs) sometimes under-perform their monolingual counterparts, possibly due to capacity limitations . We quantify this “multilingual penalty” for lexical disambiguation—a task requiring precise semantic representations and contextualization mechanisms—using controlled datasets of human relatedness judgments for ambiguous words in both English and Spanish.

pmc-11499879.creator: Yunha Nam, Byung Ju Kang, Sang-Bum Hong, Kyeongman Jeon, Dong-Hyun Lee, Jung Soo Kim, Jisoo Park, Sang-Min Lee, Song I Lee

This retrospective, multicenter cohort study included patients from nine hospitals in South Korea.
